thesis: This episode argues that Microsoft, under Satya Nadella, has transformed into a superior partner by prioritizing genuine product integration and founder collaboration over short-term financial engineering. The speaker contrasts this approach with traditional corporate acquisition strategies that focus on revenue multiples first, which often lead to long-term brand damage and a 'bag of crap'.

claims.claim: The speaker praises Microsoft as a fantastic partner under Satya Nadella, noting they delivered on promises and improved their partnership reputation compared to the Gates/Balmer era.
claims.quote: And I will say, look, with all the difficulty of the deal and Microsoft being Microsoft, they've been as good a partner. As not only we've had a Databricks but an entire portfolio, I mean, they really lived up and delivered what they said they would do

claims.claim: The speaker credits Satya Nadella with turning Microsoft into a great partner and putting Databricks on the map, stating they have been a great partner ever since.
claims.quote: So it's Kudos to Satya and they put us on the map. And he's been a great partner ever since whenever there's been issues, they always resolve it. So, you know, we're very thankful. Wouldn't be where we are without them.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that Microsoft's acquisition strategy focuses on building together with founders and integrating code bases rather than just buying revenue.
claims.quote: We're not doing that. You know, what we're really doing is, number one, we spend a lot of time with the team and the founders. So we're trying to see, hey, can we build together? Like you come here and you build together.

claims.claim: Satya Nadella explains that Microsoft avoids the 'buy revenue' model where they park waste with the CEO and kill the old company, preferring to integrate assets properly.
claims.quote: We're not doing that. You know, what we're really doing is, number one, we spend a lot of time with the team and the founders. So we're trying to see, hey, can we build together? Like you come here and you build together. That's very different from that buying revenue model.

claims.claim: Satya Nadella states that Microsoft spends time on product integration and code bases before looking at financials, unlike big corporate departments that prioritize revenue multiples first.
claims.quote: Number two, we spend a lot of time on the product. What's the product experience? How would we integrate this? What would it look like? How much can we rewrite most of it? Can we not rewrite it?

claims.claim: Satya Nadella criticizes big corporate departments for doing acquisitions in the reverse order, starting with revenue multiples and financial engineering rather than product and culture.
claims.quote: And I feel like big companies, corporate departments do exactly in the reverse order of this. They start with, hey, the revenue is this, but we could accelerate it and the multiple's so low and like, you know, in my excel sheet here, this makes perfect sense.

claims.claim: The speaker notes that while financial engineering works for some companies short-term, it creates a long-term 'bag of crap' that affects brand reputation and customer experience.
claims.quote: And it affects a brand, you know, like one of the things is, one of the reasons data breaks is so powerful is all their customers wanna buy all their products because they're like, we know that's the best software we buy.
